 England complete impressive win over Australia - as it happened
 15 November 2026 Sun 15 Nov 2026 , Men's One Day International Series - 2nd ODI Australia vs England, result Australia Australia Result England England 220 all out ( 44.3 ) 355 -6 ( 50.0 ) England   win by 135 runs Australia innings: 220 all out from 44.3 overs
 England innings: 355 for 6 from 50.0 overs
 Banton pushes case and bowlers sparkle for England 
 Live Reporting (active) 
 Scorecard 
 Summary
 England's 135-run win levels series with one to play 
 Decider in Hobart on Wednesday (03:30 GMT)
 Atkinson takes 4-28, including three with new ball
 Banton hits 121 off 99 balls as England pile up 355-6
 Cox hits inventive 67 in stand of 102 with Jacks (54*)
 Root (62) puts on 137 for second wicket with Banton
 Close form Have your say on England men this winter
 Get involved Live Reporting
 by Sam Drury & Tim Abraham
 That's all, folks! published at 11:51 GMT 15 November 11:51 GMT 15 November 
 Image source, Getty Images We're done for today after an emphatic win for England in Adelaide.
 You can read all about a Tom Banton and Gus Atkinson-inspired thrashing to level the ODI series in Matthew Henry's report. 
 We'll be back for the decider on Wednesday. Be sure to join us then!
 65 3 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 11:48 GMT 15 November 11:48 GMT 15 November 
 That's almost it from us. Just time for a quick reminder that the series decider in Hobart is coming up nice and early on Wednesday morning.
 That's followed by a five-match T20 series.
 28 4 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 11:47 GMT 15 November 11:47 GMT 15 November 
 Michael Vaughan 
Former England captain on Test Match Special 
 Tom Banton has really found his flow for batting. I don't know who the person was to say 'you can open the batting in 50-over cricket, Tom' but it's been a tremendous move. He and Ben Duckett look a good combo. 
 Banton seems to have all the time, all the strokes. He's got the pull shot, he's got the drive down the ground and he plays spin great.
 96 2 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'We looked in control the whole innings' published at 11:45 GMT 15 November 11:45 GMT 15 November 
 Image source, Getty Images England captain Harry Brook: "We put in a really good performance there, really pleasing to see us bounce back like that.
 "The whole innings, we looked like we were in control. We countered their bad balls, put them under pressure when we needed to and Tom Banton played an exceptional innings.
 "He played to his strengths and put away the bad balls. The depth that we have means we were able to go on and get that 350."
 On talks after Perth: "You want to learn from your mistakes but we knew, coming here, that this was going to be a much better wicket and thankfully some lads cashed in."
 On fielding: "That's the template we want to set every time we go out in the field. It's been a massive discussion in the group in the last year and a half.
 "We want to be one of the strongest and fittest fielding sides in the world and I thought that display out there was awesome, bar a couple of dropped catches.
 "Mis-execution you can deal with but the energy you can control."
 58 1 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'Tried some different plans' published at 11:43 GMT 15 November 11:43 GMT 15 November 
 Image source, Getty Images Australia captain Mitch Marsh: "We obviously bowled first thinking there might have been a little bit in the wicket, which probably sounds weird to say at the Adelaide Oval, and try to maximise those early overs. I thought they batted really well. We tried a lot through the 50 overs, a few different plans with Riley Meredith bowling bumpers, and all sorts of stuff. 
 "Credit to England. They played well. We know they are a good side. A really rounded side and they showed that tonight."
 On the toss: "I do bowl first a lot. Maybe I'll start batting first!"
 On why their batting struggled: "Any time you are chasing 350 you are the under pump from ball one. We needed two of our top order to really set the platform to have any chance. Credit to England, they played really well today so it's 1-1 going to Hobart."
 51 3 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'A special feeling' published at 11:39 GMT 15 November 11:39 GMT 15 November 
 Image source, Getty Images Player of the match, England's Tom Banton: "I've watched a lot of cricket in Australia over the years, the Ashes and white-ball cricket, so to come here today was a special feeling."
 On his innings: "50-over cricket is hard, sometimes you get off to a flyer then you have to rein it back in and visa-versa. It's just picking moments and match-ups."
 On partnership with Joe Root: "I've played with Rooty a little bit now and, having him at the other end, he's such a calm head and makes it much easier for me.
 "He's one of the greats of the game so to be at the other end and watch him go about his business is pretty cool."
 On his bowling: "I've been working on my bowling in the nets but it's a lot harder in a game!"
 80 6 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 How's stat?! published at 11:37 GMT 15 November 11:37 GMT 15 November 
 135 runs margin is the third-biggest win for England over Australia in ODIs. Overall, this is England's 21st biggest ODI victory in terms of runs.
 91 5 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 11:34 GMT 15 November 11:34 GMT 15 November 
 Darren Lehmann 
Ex-Australia coach on Test Match Special 
 Australia were a little bit lacklustre. They will have been disappointed to let England get over 350. They didn't quite it right with the ball. Didn't swing it enough or put it in the right areas. Having said that Tom Banton and Joe Root were excellent and set it up.
 95 11 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'Proud moment' published at 11:33 GMT 15 November 11:33 GMT 15 November 
 England batter Tom Banton, speaking to Test Match Special: "I think the most important thing is getting the win. Coming here today if we didn't win, the Hobart match wouldn't have mattered. It's been a great day and I'm very happy.
 "The toss in Perth was a big thing, they bowled well and put us under pressure. That's how cricket works sometimes. It can change really quickly. We spoke about sticking to what we know well and do well.
 "Looking back at the last ODI series we started slow and then came back stronger. It's been a great day so it'll be a nice day off tomorrow, some training then a big game on Wednesday." 
 On scoring a century in Australia: "Growing up I watched so much cricket - the Ashes, one-day cricket and T20s - so do that is a very proud moment. For me I am trying to win games for England, and do as much as I can."
 On whether he has nailed down the opener's spot: "I'd like to think so but cricket is funny old game. It can change very quickly. I'm taking each game as it comes and trying to score as many runs as I can."
 134 2 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 11:31 GMT 15 November 11:31 GMT 15 November 
 Image source, Getty Images Tom Banton was the star with the bat for England today.
 He registered his second ODI century, making 121 from 99 balls, as he and Joe Root (62 from 68) laid the foundations after the tourists were put in to bat.
 There was a slight wobble in the middle but half-centuries from Jordan Cox (67 from 49) and Will Jacks (54* from 40) ensured England posted a commanding 355-6.
 152 1 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 How's stat?! published at 11:28 GMT 15 November 11:28 GMT 15 November 
 Today, 10% of Archer's deliveries were projected to hit the stumps. Atkinson (7%) and Edwards (5%) are behind Archer today.
 100 10 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 England set up series decider published at 11:26 GMT 15 November 11:26 GMT 15 November 
 A fantastic performance from Harry Brook's side.
 They secure England's first ODI victory in Adelaide for 15 years and in fine style - thumping Australia by 135 runs.
 That levels up the series at 1-1 with the decider to come in Hobart on Wednesday.
 246 7 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 11:24 GMT 15 November 11:24 GMT 15 November 
 Darren Lehmann 
Ex-Australia coach on Test Match Special 
 England were too good. They have bounced back from Perth. Australia were outplayed in all departments apart from the fielding.
 247 10 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 ENGLAND WIN BY 135 RUNS published at 44.3 overs 44.3 overs 
 Johnson b Archer 14 (Aus 220 all out) 
 Jofra Archer finishes the job!
 Spencer Johnson was put down by Sonny Baker the ball previous, a tough chance as he sprinted in from deep third, but he's cleaned up this time.
 Full, fast and straight from Archer. Middle stump located and England secure a comprehensive win.
 1230 15 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 get involved Get Involved published at 11:21 GMT 15 November 11:21 GMT 15 November 
 Use the form on this page 
 Is there a more frustrating thing in cricket than England bowling for the 10th wicket?
 Bernard, Regua, Portugal 
 430 86 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Aus 218-9 published at 44 overs 44 overs 
 Sonny Baker is the latest bowler to have a go at taking this final wicket.
 He, too, can't manage it as a slower ball slips just past Riley Meredith's off stump.
 At this rate, the players and umpires will be the only ones left at the Adelaide Oval by the time this finishes.
 88 15 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Aus 216-9 published at 43 overs 43 overs 
 Tom Banton's, um, interesting spell is done with Jofra Archer back to try and finish this off.
 No joy this time. A maximum of seven overs before England's victory is confirmed.
 Image caption, Tom Banton's bowling pitch map
 87 6 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 get involved Get Involved published at 11:14 GMT 15 November 11:14 GMT 15 November 
 Use the form on this page 
 Can’t help thinking of the ODI against Pakistan when they had one wicket remaining…
 Simon Carr, Reading 
 144 202 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Aus 213-9 published at 42 overs 42 overs 
 Just a single from the over and Gus Atkinson is done for the day.
 He's been excellent and finishes with figures of 4-28 from his 10 overs.
 290 3 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 11:10 GMT 15 November 11:10 GMT 15 November 
 Darren Lehmann 
Ex-Australia coach on Test Match Special 
 Image source, Getty Images Australia may give Travis Head a day off in the final ODI in Hobart. It depends how they see the whole summer. He may have a week off then slot back in for the T20 series.
